title: Reading the Room: Foundations, Design, and Challenges of Normative Competence in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.10906v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human communities are governed by normative systems: shared standards that produce \textit{norms} dictating acceptable behavior, enforced through community sanctioning. Aligning increasingly autonomous AI systems with these norms is a central alignment challenge, complicated by the fact that norms are vast in number, change quickly, and are often arbitrary (e.g., dress or language conventions). Thus, alignment requires \textit{normative competence}: the ability to discern from interaction alone what norms a community enforces without relying on static pretrained knowledge. We introduce a multi-agent community debate setting, where access to debate is governed by synthetic norms, to study normative competence in isolation from pretraining exposure. translated_title: 察言观色：大语言模型规范胜任力的基础、设计与挑战
translated_abstract: 人类社群由规范系统治理：共同的标准产生规定可接受行为的“规范”，并通过社群制裁加以执行。使日益自主的AI系统与这些规范保持一致是一个核心的对齐挑战，其复杂性在于规范数量庞大、变化迅速，且往往具有任意性（例如着装或语言惯例）。因此，对齐需要“规范胜任力”：即仅凭交互便能辨别一个社群所执行的规范、而不依赖静态预训练知识的能力。我们引入了一个多智能体社群辩论场景，其中参与辩论的准入由合成规范控制，以便将规范胜任力与预训练接触隔离开来进行研究。我们证明，基线LLM智能体即使在学习规范能够提升其准确性的情况下也未能学会规范。随后，我们尝试了各种“规范模块”——作为架构组件（原摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文首次在多智能体社群辩论场景中研究大语言模型的“规范胜任力”——即仅凭交互识别社群规范而不依赖预训练知识的能力，并发现基线LLM智能体即使学会规范有利可图也无法掌握规范。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a multi-agent community debate setting to study normative competence in LLMs—the ability to discern a community's norms from interaction alone without relying on pretrained knowledge—and shows that baseline LLM agents fail to learn norms even when doing so would improve their accuracy.
